ledger.note: 1717: Farrukhsiyar recognises Murshid Quli Khan as hereditary Nawab Nazim of Bengal, and Bengal becomes a de facto independent state with its capital at Murshidabad. 'In 1717, Mughal emperor Farrukhsiyar recognized Khan as the hereditary Nawab Nazim. The Nawab's jurisdiction covered districts in Bengal, Bihar, and Orissa.' The Bengal Subah page adds 'By the 18th century, Bengal emerged as a de facto independent state' (infobox 1717-1757) while the nawabs 'continued to issue coins in the name of the Mughal Emperor'. The core drawn is Bengal and Orissa; Bihar is dated to 1733 by the same page's table. Fix fx-10 (1 Nov 2026): without the Tripura hills and the Chittagong Hill Tracts. Kingdom of Tripura page (opened 2026-11-01): 'the Mughals could never penetrate the Hills territories to the east', only the plains fell to them; History of Chittagong page: the Mughals annexed Chatgaon (the port) in 1666 and the page does not say the Hill Tracts were ever Mughal. The Nawabs inherit Mughal Bengal, so Cliopatria's shape over the hills is dropped (kingdom-of-tripura keeps them).

1733: the Bihar subah is annexed to the Nawabs' territory. The page's table lists 'Annexation of the Bihar Subah into the territory of the nawabs of Bengal' under 1733; the page's prose already says the 1717 jurisdiction covered Bihar, and Cliopatria draws Bihar from 1718.

1740: Alivardi Khan takes the throne, ending the Nasiri dynasty of Murshid Quli Khan and his heirs. Rulers table: Sarfaraz Khan to 29 April 1740, Alivardi Khan from 29 April 1740; the Giria entry says he 'takes the throne, ending the Nasiri dynasty'. Same state, same colour (rule 2).

region.text: Orissa, the province entered by the Maratha armies and recovered by Alivardi Khan in 1749

ledger.note: 1742: the Marathas of Raghuji Bhonsle invade Bengal through Orissa. 'In April, Maratha forces under Bhaskar Ram sent by Raghuji Bhonsle to collect chauth tribute, invaded Bengal via Odisha' (April 1742); 'Between April 1742 to March 1751, the Marathas invaded Bengal five times in 1742, 1743, 1744, 1745 and 1748'. The page does not say which Orissa districts were held in which year; the zone is the researcher's reading, supported by the Nawabs page's 1749 entry 'Orissa recovered; Fort surrendered to the Nawab' (Siege of Cuttack).

region.text: Orissa, under a governor appointed under the treaty, de facto Maratha

ledger.note: 1751: peace with the Marathas ends the invasions. 'The agreement was formally signed with the approval of the Nagpur court in May or June 1751'; 'Marathas agreed to never cross the Subarnarekha River'; from October 1751 the Nawab pays 1.2 million rupees a year as chauth of Bengal and Bihar. Mir Habib 'was made provincial governor of Orissa under nominal control of the Nawab of Bengal': 'de facto Maratha control over Orissa was established by 1751'.

region.text: Orissa, 'formally incorporated in the Maratha Empire in 1752'

ledger.note: 1752: Orissa is formally incorporated in the Maratha dominion. The Nawabs page: Orissa 'was formally incorporated in the Maratha Empire in 1752'; the Maratha invasions page: after Mir Habib was assassinated in 1752 'the Marathas formally incorporated Orissa in their dominion' (the Nagpur kingdom of the Bhonsles). A January 1747 date on the Nawabs page ('persuaded the Emperor to cede Orissa to the Marathas') does not fit the 1749 recovery and is not used.

region.text: the land within the Maratha Ditch and 'the zamindari of all the land between Calcutta and the sea' granted to the Company

ledger.note: 1757: the Company takes the land around Calcutta. After Plassey 'the British acquired all the land within the Maratha Ditch and 600 yards (550 m) beyond it' and 'the zamindari of all the land between Calcutta and the sea'; Cliopatria's British Empire shape of 1757 (2,782 km2 inside the Nawabs' 1752 shape) is the strip drawn. The page dates the treaty with Mir Jafar to 4 June 1757 (the grant took effect after Plassey, 23 June 1757) and does not name the 24 Parganas.

Battle of Plassey infobox (opened 2 Nov 2026): 'Mir Jafar becomes the Nawab of Bengal and Bengal becomes a British puppet state'; territorial changes 'Bengal came under de facto control of the British East India Company'; 'Clive placed Mir Jafar on the throne'. The Nawabs of Bengal page: 'On 23 June 1757, the Battle of Plassey brought an end to the independence of the nawabs of Bengal' and 'Mir Jafar was installed as the puppet Nawab by the British'. Recorded from the vassal's side (counterpart = overlord); british-empire/ledger/2 is the mirror. Fix fx-40 (2 Nov 2026), R095: the dossier used to end here with a dissolve, which drew Bengal and Bihar as direct British land from 1757; the line of nawabs went on as a client until the Diwani (see the dissolve of 1765).

region.text: the Nawab's Bengal and Bihar, a British client from Plassey, the Company's by the Diwani of 1765

ledger.note: 16 August 1765: the Diwani ends the Nawabs' separate state. Nawabs of Bengal page (opened 2 Nov 2026): 'In 1765, Robert Clive, as the representative of the East India Company, was given the Diwani of Bengal'; 'With this a system of dual governance was established, with the nawabs responsible for the Nizamat of Bengal'; 'In 1772, this arrangement came to be abolished and Bengal was brought under direct control of the British'; 'The nawabs had lost all independent authority since 1757.' Treaty of Allahabad page: 'The Treaty of Allahabad was signed on 16 August 1765'; Shah Alam 'granted the East India Company Diwani rights, or the right to collect taxes on behalf of the Emperor' in Bengal and Bihar (the page does not mention the Nawab or the Nizamat). british-empire/ledger/9 ends the client relation on the same date. The line of nawabs goes on (Najmuddin Ali Khan from 5 February 1765, the Nizamat to 1772, the title abolished 1880) without independent authority. Fix fx-40, R095: was a dissolve of 23 June 1757 (Plassey), which made the whole shape British land for eight years; the 1757 client relation is now the vassal_start above.

wars.name: Maratha invasions of Bengal

zones.text: Orissa, where Maratha control was de facto by 1751

wars.outcome: Five invasions (1742, 1743, 1744, 1745 and 1748). The peace of May or June 1751 fixes the Subarnarekha as the limit, sets 1.2 million rupees a year as the chauth of Bengal and Bihar and leaves Orissa under Mir Habib, a governor under nominal Nawab control; the Marathas incorporate Orissa formally in 1752.
wars.note: The raids reached western Bengal and Bihar ('The further attacks took place in 1748 in Bihar'), but the page names no ground held outside Orissa, so only Orissa is a contest zone. Territory south of the Subarnarekha is the infobox's 'ceded into the Nagpur State'.

wars.name: Siraj-ud-Daulah's war with the East India Company and the Battle of Plassey

zones.text: Calcutta and the land between Calcutta and the sea

wars.outcome: 'On 20 June 1756, Nawab Siraj-ud-Daulah launched the siege of Calcutta, in which he won a decisive victory'; Clive took Chandannagar from the French on 24 March 1757 and won at Plassey on 23 June 1757. Mir Jafar became puppet Nawab; the Company acquired the land within the Maratha Ditch and the zamindari between Calcutta and the sea.
wars.note: The retaking of Calcutta (early 1757) is not dated on the pages opened.

certainty.note: Subah and district limits, no survey. The Subarnarekha river limit with the Marathas is a treaty line from 1751 (sharp on that stretch only); the Calcutta strip granted in 1757 is defined by the Maratha Ditch and the sea.

Cliopatria's 1757 shape (to 1761) held as the client Nawabdom's extent to the Diwani; no page opened draws its borders, and the cession of Chittagong, Burdwan and Midnapore to the Company by Mir Qasim (after October 1760) is not placed.

notes: Budget: 5 pages, all used. Cliopatria rows: one Name, 'Nawabs of Bengal' 1718-1761; the BD Seshat id bd_nawabs_of_bengal was not opened. Corrections: (1) Cliopatria draws Bihar from 1718 and leaves Odisha out; the Nawabs page puts Orissa in the 1717 jurisdiction and dates the annexation of Bihar to 1733, so Bihar is removed 1718-1732 and Odisha added to 1751, with the Maratha contest in Odisha 1742-1751 and formal loss 1752 (Cliopatria's Maratha shape of 1752 holds Odisha). The page's prose also names Bihar in 1717; the disagreement is recorded, the dated table entry is followed. (2) The state ends in June 1757 (Plassey: 'brought an end to the independence of the nawabs'), not 1761; Cliopatria's British Empire takes the Bengal shape in 1762. The 1757-1761 shape is a British client. A vassal_start for the Nawab belongs in the british-empire dossier (counterpart nawabs-of-bengal, 1757); this dossier cannot carry the suzerain's event. Not on the pages opened (left out, not filled from memory): the Mir Qasim cession of Burdwan, Midnapore and Chittagong in 1760 (Buxar page silent), the retaking of Calcutta in 1757, the date of the post-Plassey treaty, the 24 Parganas, Dhaka's role. The Nawabs page's table lists Najmuddin Ali Khan from 5 February 1765, but he reigns after the end of the sovereign state and is not in the ruler strip. Nominal Mughal sovereignty (coins in the emperor's name, the 1717 recognition, the 1765 Diwani) is not drawn as a vassal tint: Cliopatria has no relation row and the Bengal Subah page gives no end date for it. Disagreements: Murshidabad as capital from 1711 (Bengal Subah infobox) or 1716 (Nawabs page); infobox abolition 1882 versus text 1880; Orissa cession January 1747 (Nawabs page footnote) versus de facto 1751 and formal 1752. Counterparts: the Bhonsles of Nagpur, who took Orissa, are not a Cliopatria row; counterpart given as maratha-empire; a dossier 'nagpur-kingdom' (Bhonsle) is needed from sa-05-x. Gazetteer: 'Murshidabad' is not a place in places.jsonl (24.18 N, 88.27 E). [Reviewer sa-05-e, 2026-10-25] The war 'Battle of Buxar' (1764-1765) was removed from wars because it lies outside the life (1717-1757); nawab-of-awadh carries it and british-empire should. Ledger 6 (the Calcutta grant) dated June 1757: the Plassey page dates the treaty with Mir Jafar to 4 June 1757. [Fix fx-40, 2 Nov 2026, R095] The state now ends on 16 August 1765, not at Plassey: Plassey makes Bengal a British puppet state (vassal_start 1757/6, mirror of british-empire/ledger/2), and the Diwani of 1765 (british-empire/ledger/9, vassal_end) ends the separate state; the shape of the 1757 keyframe holds to 1765. Not added: Mir Qasim's cession of Chittagong, Burdwan and Midnapore to the Company ('In one of his first acts', after October 1760; the page gives no year for it beyond 'in October 1760' for the change of Nawab, and no extent).
